source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Where you find a "F" (for failed) in a slot - make a note of the column and row that has the F in it.
3. Take the column and row and refer to the details on page 4. This will tell you what is wrong with the appliance.
5. The most common problem which causes an appliance to fail the PAT test is the earth continuity.
6. When performing a PAT test we look for 2 things "a live" and "an earth". If we find the appliance is not earth bonded correctly (usually because there is no earth wire on the plug) or there is internal damage to the wires within the appliance we have a problem. If the appliance fails the test we can't consider it safe to use.
7. The most common fix for these failed appliances is re-wiring the plug. This cost $12.50 + GST.
